gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Epoch 12V 105Ah Essential Heated starts its heater with as little as 0.5 A of incoming charge current and never uses its stored energy for the heater. It also isn't stated that Battle Born's heater pulls about 28 W from the battery's own cells once a charge source is present below about 35°F. The rival pages give only Renogy's 4 A and LiTime's 10 A thresholds.
standout_why: I compared four pages. BatteryTrail's spec database (cited) gives only Renogy's heater threshold, 'more than 4A per battery', and says no minimum current is published for any other model. CompareFoundry (cited) gives LiTime's 10 A Regular-mode minimum, its battery-powered mode above 20% SOC, and Renogy's 4 A, but nothing for Epoch or Battle Born. Boondockmaps (cited) says only that the Epoch 'heats itself' to -4°F and gives no power source or current. GearRanking (cited) would not load because of an SSL certificate error, so I could not compare against it. ChatGPT's answer carried only the general caveat that 'some models require incoming charging current'.
decides: What decides whether the plan works is whether the shopper's winter charge source supplies enough current to start the heater. A weak morning solar trickle or a small maintainer can warm the Epoch, which needs 0.5 A. The same source may never wake the LiTime, which needs 10 A in Regular mode, or the Renogy Pro, which needs more than 4 A per battery, so those packs sit unable to charge. That supports keeping Epoch as the pick for solar-only or low-amp setups. Battle Born works the other way: its heater runs on the battery's own cells, but only once a charge source is present, so it can warm up from a tiny charge source at the cost of about 28 W from the pack. Owners need to know that.

findings.note: Maker page: 'Charging disabled at 0°C / 32°F; resumes automatically at 5°C / 41°F'; charge range '−20°C to 55°C / −4°F to 131°F, with heating'.

findings.value: The battery's own cells, and only when a charge source is present
findings.source_title: How Battle Born Heated Batteries Work | The Battle Born Educational Series (2026-04-28)
findings.note: Maker: 'The heater draws power from the battery itself, not from an external source'; it activates when the internal temperature drops to about 35°F and 'a charge source is present'.

findings.label: Heater draw while on
findings.source_title: How Battle Born Heated Batteries Work | The Battle Born Educational Series (2026-04-28)
findings.note: Maker: 'typically around 28 watts when active'. At 12.8 V that is about 2.2 A from the pack (28 / 12.8).

findings.label: Minimum charge current to start the heater
findings.value: More than 4 A per battery in the bank; heats from charger power below 41°F
findings.source_title: LiFePO4 RV Battery Spec Database – BatteryTrail
findings.note: BatteryTrail: 'Heater runs from charger at -4°F to 41°F', and the heater activates only when the charger supplies more than 4 A per battery. CompareFoundry says the same ('stable charge current above 4 A'). Renogy's own page returned HTTP 429.

findings.label: Minimum charge current to start the heater, and battery-powered mode
findings.value: At least 10 A in Regular mode; Energy-efficient mode can heat from the battery above 20% SOC; heats between -4°F and 41°F (-20°C to 5°C)
findings.source_title: Choose a 12V LiFePO4 battery: capacity, BMS limits, cold charging and US packages – CompareFoundry
findings.note: CompareFoundry: needs 'a charger of at least 10 A in its Regular mode'; Energy-efficient mode 'can draw battery power above 20% SOC'. LiTime's own page returned HTTP 429.
